predecessors.name: Landgraviate of Thuringia
predecessors.text: Hesse, split from Thuringia in the War of the Thuringian Succession: 'Partitioned from Duchy of Thuringia: 1264'

successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel
successors.text: 'His eldest son William IV inherited the northern half of the Landgraviate and the capital of Kassel' (Hesse-Kassel page)

successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt
successors.text: George, the youngest son, 'received the Hessian lands in the former upper County of Katzenelnbogen' (Hesse-Darmstadt page)

successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Marburg
successors.text: Upper Hesse round Marburg, Louis IV's share

successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Rheinfels
successors.text: the lower County of Katzenelnbogen on the Middle Rhine, Philip II's share

ledger.x: 1264: Henry I the Child becomes the first Landgrave of Hesse.
1308: Hesse is divided into Upper and Lower Hesse until 1311.
1311: the two halves are joined again (end of the first division).
1458: the second division into Upper and Lower Hesse begins (to 1500).
1479: the Upper County of Katzenelnbogen comes to Hesse.
1567: Hesse is divided among four sons.
1567: the Landgraviate of Hesse ends in the four-way partition; the Rheinfels line dies out in 1583 and the Marburg line in 1604, both 'incorporated into Hesse-Kassel' (and Darmstadt for Marburg).

wars.name: War of the Thuringian Succession
wars.outcome: Brabant keeps Hesse ('This created the Landgraviate of Hesse'); the Margrave of Meissen takes Thuringia and the title of Landgrave of Thuringia.

certainty.note: The page names seats and the Upper/Lower division, no boundaries; the Katzenelnbogen lands were detached enclaves.
